FROM ORDERS o JOIN PRODUCTS p ON p.ID = o.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE p.CATEGORY = {{category}}
GROUP BY p.CATEGORY

tables.caveats: Piespace’s business operates with a two week trial period. If you see that “Canceled At” is null then that account is still happily paying for their pies.
tables.description: Information on customer accounts registered with Piespace. Each account represents a new organization signing up for on-demand pies.
tables.name: ACCOUNTS
tables.points_of_interest: Is it? We’ll let you be the judge of that.

tables.caveats: Piespace has cracked time travel, so keep in mind that some events may have already happened in the future.
tables.description: Piespace does some anonymous analytics tracking on how users interact with their platform. They’ve only had time to implement a few events, but you know how it is. Pies come first.
tables.name: ANALYTIC_EVENTS
tables.points_of_interest: Is it? We’ll let you be the judge of that.

tables.caveats: Not every account feels inclined to submit feedback. That’s cool. There’s still quite a few responses here.
tables.description: With each order of pies sent out, Piespace includes a place for customers to submit feedback and review their order.
tables.name: FEEDBACK

tables.caveats: You can group by “Account ID” to see all the payments from an account and unveil information like total amount paid to date.

fields.description: This is a unique ID for the product. It is also called the “Invoice number” or “Confirmation number” in customer facing emails and screens.
fields.name: ID

fields.description: The id of the user who made this order. Note that in some cases where an order was created on behalf of a customer who phoned the order in, this might be the employee who handled the request.
fields.name: USER_ID

target.description: A unique identifier given to each user.
target.name: ID

fields.description: The product ID. This is an internal identifier for the product, NOT the SKU.
fields.name: PRODUCT_ID

target.description: The numerical product number. Only used internally. All external communication should use the title or EAN.
target.name: ID

fields.description: The raw, pre-tax cost of the order. Note that this might be different in the future from the product price due to promotions, credits, etc.
fields.name: SUBTOTAL

fields.description: This is the amount of local and federal taxes that are collected on the purchase. Note that other governmental fees on some products are not included here, but instead are accounted for in the subtotal.
fields.name: TAX

fields.description: The total billed amount.
fields.name: TOTAL

fields.description: Discount amount.
fields.name: DISCOUNT

fields.description: The date and time an order was submitted.
fields.name: CREATED_AT

fields.description: Number of products bought.
fields.name: QUANTITY

segments.definition_description: Filtered by Total is greater than 100
segments.name: Big Orders

cols.description: The type of product, valid values include: Doohicky, Gadget, Gizmo and Widget
cols.name: CATEGORY

native_form.query: SELECT "Products"."CATEGORY" AS "Products__CATEGORY", SUM("ORDERS"."TOTAL") AS "sum" FROM "ORDERS" LEFT JOIN (SELECT "PRODUCTS"."ID" AS "ID", "PRODUCTS"."EAN" AS "EAN", "PRODUCTS"."TITLE" AS "TITLE", "PRODUCTS"."CATEGORY" AS "CATEGORY", "PRODUCTS"."VENDOR" AS "VENDOR", "PRODUCTS"."PRICE" AS "PRICE", "PRODUCTS"."RATING" AS "RATING", "PRODUCTS"."CREATED_AT" AS "CREATED_AT" FROM "PRODUCTS") AS "Products" ON "ORDERS"."PRODUCT_ID" = "Products"."ID" GROUP BY "Products"."CATEGORY" ORDER BY "Products"."CATEGORY" ASC

columns.description: The type of product, valid values include: Doohicky, Gadget, Gizmo and Widget
columns.name: CATEGORY

native_form.query:
SELECT p.CATEGORY, count(*) AS ORDERS, sum(o.TOTAL) AS REVENUE, max(o.CREATED_AT) AS LAST_ORDER
FROM ORDERS o JOIN PRODUCTS p ON p.ID = o.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE p.CATEGORY = ?
GROUP BY p.CATEGORY
